result:
I changed `GET /orders` so each order now includes an `items` array. I couldn't run the tests because `npm test` was denied approval in this session, so none of this has been run.

Each item has `product_id`, `product_name`, `quantity` and `price_cents`. The price is what the order paid, taken from `order_items`, not the product's current price. The change is in `src/app.ts`. It's still one query per request: it joins `order_items` and `products` and builds the array in Postgres. An order with no items gets `items: []`, and items are sorted by product id.

I also added a test in `test/app.test.ts` that checks `items` is an array and that each item has exactly those four fields. It doesn't check the item values.

If you approve `npm test`, or run it yourself, that will confirm it works. I haven't updated the Postman collection or the README. I didn't check whether the Postman collection documents the `/orders` response shape.
